subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: Should OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical requests within one reviewer/run, and what exact cache key, lifetime, and outcome set are acceptable on the exec approval boundary?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but the fix changes one-request-one-model-review semantics on a command execution approval path, which is a security-boundary policy choice rather than a purely mechanical optimization.

options.title: Approve bounded exact-input memo
options.body: Allow a small per-reviewer-instance cache keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, with tests for key separation, eviction, and unchanged allow-once handling.

options.title: Cache only low-risk allows
options.body: Permit memoization only for parsed low-risk allow-once verdicts and keep ask, timeout, error, and unavailable-model outcomes uncached.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Reject reviewer-result caching for now and accept repeated reviewer completions until a different cost-control design is chosen.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded exact-input memo
recommendation.body: Allow a small per-reviewer-instance cache keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, with tests for key separation, eviction, and unchanged allow-once handling.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent exec approval and security allowlist history makes this the strongest available owner signal for the approval-boundary decision.
